name: Phish to foothold
team_objective: Red gains a controlled foothold; Blue validates user report and endpoint containment.

objectives.text: Establish controlled execution and prove access.
Validate alert, scope, contain, and preserve evidence.

injects.text: Synthetic user reports a suspicious attachment.
Optional hint: check process lineage under the mail client.

learning.overview: Trace a phishing intrusion from the initial lure to code execution on the endpoint, and learn what evidence a defender collects.
concepts: Initial access often starts with a benign-looking attachment or link (T1566).
Execution shows up as a process spawned by an unusual parent (e.g. a mail client).
Defenders correlate mail, endpoint, and process-lineage evidence on one timeline.

steps.title: Deliver the phishing lure
steps.instructions: Run the phishing delivery. A benign attachment lands in the seeded mailbox.

steps.title: Observe code execution
steps.instructions: Run the interpreter module to emulate the payload executing.
steps.observe: Watch the process-execution events land on the timeline.

quiz.q: Which tactic does a phishing attachment map to?
quiz.explain: Phishing (T1566) is an Initial Access technique.

quiz.q: A strong endpoint signal of a malicious document is…
options: An office/mail app spawning a shell or interpreter
quiz.explain: Unusual parent→child process lineage (e.g. Outlook → powershell) is the tell.

name: Identity compromise
team_objective: Investigate seeded password reuse and remote logons; revoke sessions and reset identities.

objectives.text: Reuse seeded credentials to move between hosts.
Detect reuse, revoke sessions, reset identities.

injects.text: Correlate logon types across the server zone.

learning.overview: Investigate credential reuse and remote logons; learn to revoke sessions and reset compromised identities.
concepts: Reused credentials let an attacker authenticate to multiple hosts (T1078).
Account and remote-system discovery precede lateral movement.
Response = revoke sessions and reset the affected identities.

steps.title: Observe credential reuse
steps.instructions: Run the seeded password-reuse module to generate remote logons.
steps.observe: Successive remote logons with the same credential.

quiz.q: Valid-account abuse maps to which technique?
quiz.explain: T1078 is the use of legitimate credentials by an adversary.

name: Ransomware precursor
team_objective: Detect discovery, staging, and safe canary encryption; contain before impact.

objectives.text: Stage collection and trigger canary encryption.

learning.overview: Recognize the precursors to ransomware — discovery, staging, and a safe canary-encryption event — and contain before impact.
concepts: Ransomware is preceded by discovery and collection/staging of files.
Impact (T1486) is a rapid burst of file modifications — here confined to canary files.
Early containment during staging prevents the impact stage.

steps.title: Spot discovery & staging
steps.instructions: Run the collection module to stage tagged files.

steps.title: Detect canary encryption
steps.instructions: Run the safe canary-encryption simulation (instructor/admin only).
steps.observe: A burst of file modifications confined to the canary directory (T1486).

quiz.q: What ATT&CK technique represents the ransomware impact stage?
Why detect during discovery/staging rather than impact?
options: Containment before impact prevents data loss
quiz.explain: Catching precursors lets you contain before files are encrypted.

name: Web app intrusion
team_objective: Trace a preconfigured vulnerable Linux app path to host activity and data access.

objectives.text: Exploit the app path and reach host data.
Trace the entry, scope host activity, and contain.

learning.overview: Follow a vulnerable web application from an exploited request to activity and data access on the host.
concepts: Web exploitation (T1190) can lead to a process spawned by the app server.
Follow the app-spawned process tree to scope host activity.
Data access shows as reads of sensitive files after the intrusion.

steps.title: Exploit the app path
steps.instructions: Run the web-app entry module and watch for an app-spawned process.
steps.observe: Web access anomaly and a child process on the app host.

steps.title: Trace host execution
steps.instructions: Run the Linux interpreter module to emulate follow-on execution.
steps.observe: Interpreter/id activity on the timeline (may fire T1059).

quiz.q: Exploiting a public-facing web app maps to which technique?
quiz.explain: T1190 covers exploiting an internet-facing application.

name: Docker compromise
team_objective: Investigate a vulnerable container, exposed synthetic secret, abnormal runtime activity, and safe host-boundary test.

objectives.text: Enumerate, access the secret, and run the boundary test.
Detect runtime anomalies and the boundary test via Falco.

learning.overview: Learn how attackers operate inside containers and how defenders detect them. You'll run real container behaviors and watch detections fire on live telemetry.
concepts: Containers share the host kernel — enumeration reveals cgroups, mounts, and capabilities.
Runtime activity like spawning a shell or writing a binary is abnormal for a service container.
A container escape probes the boundary to the host (docker socket, sensitive mounts, privilege).

steps.title: Enumerate the container
steps.instructions: Run container enumeration and read the timeline. Notice the cgroup, mount table, and capability set the process can see.
steps.observe: A DR-CONTAINER-DISCOVERY detection (T1613) fires from a real log line.

steps.title: Trigger abnormal runtime activity
steps.instructions: Run the runtime module. It spawns a nested shell and writes/executes a payload inside the container.
steps.observe: DR-CONTAINER-RUNTIME-EXEC (T1610) fires — note the MTTD (detection latency).

steps.title: Probe the host boundary
steps.instructions: Run the safe boundary test. It checks for docker-socket exposure and sensitive host mounts.
steps.observe: DR-HOST-ESCAPE (T1611) fires; the boundary correctly holds (no host access).

quiz.q: Which ATT&CK technique covers discovering the container/orchestration context?
quiz.explain: T1613 covers enumerating containers, images, and their resources.

quiz.q: What makes an interactive shell inside a service container suspicious?
options: It is normal for web servers
Service containers should not spawn interactive shells
quiz.explain: A hands-on shell inside a single-purpose service container is a strong signal of compromise.

quiz.q: MTTD reported by the detection engine measures…
options: Time from the activity to the detection firing
quiz.explain: MTTD (mean time to detect) is the latency between the observed activity and the verdict.

name: Insider collection
team_objective: Distinguish legitimate access from abnormal synthetic-data collection.

objectives.text: Separate normal from abnormal collection and act.

learning.overview: Distinguish legitimate access from abnormal synthetic-data collection by an insider.
concepts: Insiders already hold valid access — behavior, not access, is the signal.
Bulk reads of tagged files plus archiving indicate collection (T1005/T1560).
Volume anomalies to unusual destinations indicate exfiltration.

steps.title: Generate collection activity
steps.instructions: Run the collection module to read and archive tagged files.

quiz.q: For an insider, the primary detection signal is…
quiz.explain: Insiders have access; you detect anomalous behavior, not the access itself.

name: Purple detection sprint
team_objective: Replay Windows, Linux, and Docker behaviors; tune rules and demonstrate improved coverage.

objectives.text: Replay across platforms and improve coverage vs baseline.

learning.overview: Replay behaviors across Windows, Linux, and Docker, then measure how detection coverage improves versus a baseline.
concepts: Purple teaming pairs execution with detection tuning.
Improvement is measured baseline→replay, not win/lose.
Log-basis detections (real evidence) are higher fidelity than technique-coverage.

steps.title: Replay a Linux behavior
steps.instructions: Run the Linux interpreter module and note which detections fire.
steps.observe: Detections recorded with a log or technique basis.

steps.title: Replay a Docker behavior
steps.instructions: Run the container runtime module for a real, high-fidelity detection.
steps.observe: A log-basis detection with measured MTTD.

quiz.explain: Purple exercises report coverage improvement, never a win/lose score.
